title: Aldervale Mutual Assurance producer counter cards: neutralize nine mixed-light agent headshots to an in-frame grey card, triage-prep the three production-tier seals, vectorize the wordmark, and data-merge one press-ready branch card per producer

source.reference: InDesign Data Merge - insurance branch producer credential / counter cards

grounding_note: Adapted from a real Freelancer.com brand-collateral brief (a regional broker wanting a fixed brand-locked template populated from a structured roster into a press-ready PDF plus an editable source, with 'the colors, fonts and overall layout from the brand style guide coming through clearly' and 'I don't want to hunt for missing fonts or mismatched data') and laundered to a fictional brand, 'Aldervale Mutual Assurance' — no real company, carrier, person, product or trademark is named anywhere; the prior 'Beacon Mutual Insurance Group' collided with a real Rhode Island carrier and is fully removed. REPOSITIONED for connector reality: the killed original tried to land a 10-12-row premium table on ONE page and routed the template through convert_pdf_to_indd — both impossible, because document_merge_data_layout emits exactly ONE FILE PER ROW (it cannot place several records on one page) and a converted-PDF template carries no live merge fields to bind. So the client is modeled as needing what the merge tool genuinely produces: a per-PRODUCER branch counter card (one A6 single-record card per licensed agent) for the branch counters and the producer directory — the finance-vertical analogue of a per-SKU line sheet, with the agent's own prepped imagery on each. The client supplies: a genuinely hand-authored InDesign single-record counter-card template (.indd, NOT a converted PDF) carrying live <<fields>> plus THREE @-prefixed image-path columns (agent headshot, production-tier seal, brand wordmark); the producer roster as a CSV; nine raw agent headshots shot across two branch open-days under mismatched light each with a photographic 18% grey card laid in frame at camera scale; the three production-tier seals (two flat two-colour crests and one photograph of an embossed metallic-foil presentation seal); and a flat printed wordmark on cream letterhead stock. The Adobe chain does the real work the brief rewards: neutralize every headshot to its own in-frame grey card so the whole producer set shares one white point and prints sharp, triage the three tier seals so each is prepped the correct way (the flat crests vectorized for razor edges, the photographed foil seal knocked to transparency and kept as high-res raster rather than destroyed by a trace), prep-and-vectorize the wordmark, then run the authored template through a one-file-per-row data-merge and export a press-ready card per producer.
one_line_ask: Neutralize nine mixed-lighting agent headshots to the 18% grey card each one carries so the producer set reads as one matched, print-sharp series, decide per frame how far to move white balance and exposure to hit the shared target without pushing any face off its real skin tone, prep the three production-tier seals each the correct way for print (the flat crests are not the same problem as the photographed foil seal), vectorize the wordmark, then data-merge the client's authored single-record InDesign counter-card template against the producer roster to produce one press-ready branch card per agent.
full_brief: Aldervale Mutual Assurance is a regional personal-lines broker, and for our branch counters and the internal producer directory we need physical producer cards — one A6 card per licensed agent, carrying that agent's name, branch, licence number, product line, direct line and their production tier, with their headshot, their tier seal and our wordmark. Our brand and the card layout are already signed off; what we need is the production pass. We are handing you everything the job needs. First, the headshots: nine agent photos, but here is the problem — they were shot at two different branch open-days by whoever had the camera, under whatever light was in the room (some under cool LED ceiling panels, some under warm reception tungsten, one under greenish back-office fluorescents, a couple over- or under-exposed), so straight out of the folder they look like nine different shoots. A rack of producer cards where every face has a different colour cast looks amateur and off-brand. To make this checkable we laid a photographic 18% grey card into the corner of every shot. Your job on the photos: bring every headshot to one consistent, true-to-skin look by neutralizing each one to the grey card it contains — the card must read as a clean neutral grey (equal across the channels) in your finished frame, and once every card is neutral the whole set shares one white point and one exposure feel. Do NOT force one blanket correction across all nine: each was lit differently and needs its own white-balance and exposure decision to land on the shared target — some frames need warming, others cooling, one needs the green pulled out on the tint axis, a couple need real exposure recovery. And be careful with skin: at least one of our agents has a genuinely warm, deep complexion and was shot under clean neutral light, so that frame's grey card already reads neutral — do not 'cool' it chasing a cast that is not there, or you will strip the real skin tone and the card will look wrong. When you are done, tell us the final white-balance and exposure move you made on each frame, and the final pixel size of each headshot, so we can confirm the set is matched and that every face will still be sharp at print size. That last part matters: each card drops the headshot into a 40 x 50 mm photo window, and at press resolution that window needs at least ~472 x 591 px of real image — a face cropped down to a small thumbnail will print soft and blurry, which we will reject. Second, the tier seals: three of them sit on the cards depending on the agent's production tier — Standard, Preferred and President's Council. They all need to drop cleanly into the card's seal window and stay razor-sharp at print size and keep their finish — but they did not all come to you as the same kind of file, and treating them all the same way will quietly wreck one of them. Look at each before you decide how to prep it. Third, our wordmark: it only exists as a flat printed mark on a piece of cream letterhead, slightly skewed on the scan with paper margin around it — get it clean, straight and razor-sharp for the card, not a fuzzy paper-bounded scan. Finally, build the cards: we have hand-built the InDesign counter-card template with the real placeholder fields and three image slots (headshot, tier seal and wordmark), and we are giving you the producer roster; merge them so every agent gets their own single card with their details bound in verbatim, their neutralized headshot in the photo window, their correct tier seal in the seal window and the wordmark in the masthead — then hand back a press-ready ~300 DPI A6 PDF, one card per producer. Bind the names, branches, licence numbers, product lines, tiers and direct lines exactly from the roster — do not invent, reassign or reformat anyone; some agent names are long and must fit the auto-size name frame without clipping. Acceptance: every grey card neutral and the whole set on one white point with no face pushed off its true skin tone; every headshot at least ~472 x 591 px so it prints >=300 DPI in the 40 x 50 mm window; the three tier seals each prepped the correct way and razor-sharp at print size; the wordmark a clean straight vector; and exactly one finished card per roster row.

inputs.name: aldervale_countercard_template.indd
inputs.gen_prompt: AUTHORED DELIVERABLE (cannot be model-generated): a genuine, hand-built Adobe InDesign document (.indd/.idml) for a SINGLE-RECORD 105 x 148 mm (A6) portrait producer counter card with 3 mm bleed — ONE producer per page — brand-locked to the Aldervale style guide (Aldervale Ink #17233A deep navy, Ember Gold #E0A43B accent, a geometric grotesque headline face and a transitional serif body face carried inside the .indd's own font resources). It must contain live InDesign data-merge placeholder fields <<agent_name>>, <<branch>>, <<license_no>>, <<product_line>>, <<tier>>, <<direct_line>>, and THREE @-prefixed image-path merge columns wired to three separate image frames: a 40 x 50 mm portrait photo window bound to @Headshot, a 22 x 22 mm square seal window bound to @Seal, and a masthead mark frame bound to @Wordmark. Because free-form image-at-coordinates placement is banned, the headshot, the tier seal AND the wordmark each reach the card ONLY as a merge bind through their image frame — none is dropped in by hand. The <<agent_name>> text frame has Auto-Size 'shrink text to fit' enabled so long producer names bind without going overset. The navy header band, the Ember-gold tier rule and the fixed card furniture are already drawn into the template artwork. Built by hand in InDesign so the merge fields and all THREE image fields actually bind. Explicitly NOT a convert_pdf_to_indd output and NOT a multi-record grid: document_merge_data_layout emits one file per row, so the template holds exactly one record's worth of fields; a converted-PDF template (no live merge fields, no data-merge image field) or a multi-up table would not bind / cannot be produced — those were the killed original's defects.
inputs.realism_notes: document_merge_data_layout is [T] and REQUIRES a user-authored .indd carrying real merge fields plus genuine @image-path columns, and it emits ONE FILE PER ROW — so a single-record per-producer counter card is the correct, connector-doable shape (one pass per agent), not a multi-row rate table on one page. Supplied as an input, not a chain output; a PDF-converted .indd with literal typed text would not bind. THREE image columns (@Headshot, @Seal, @Wordmark) mean the merge must resolve three prepped assets per row — the row's neutralized headshot, its mapped tier seal, and the shared vectorized wordmark — so every chain-produced asset has a real, connector-doable path onto each card via the merge, never free-form placement. Column names must exactly match the roster headers and the template fields.

inputs.name: aldervale_producer_roster.csv
inputs.gen_prompt: Generate a CSV with headers exactly: agent_name,branch,license_no,product_line,tier,direct_line,@Headshot,@Seal,@Wordmark and 9 producer rows (one per licensed agent). agent_name is a mix of realistic international names including at least two DELIBERATELY LONG names (e.g. 'Marguerite Featherstonehaugh-Okwu', ~28+ chars) alongside short ones so the template's shrink-to-fit is exercised. branch is one of a few fictional branch names ('Harbour Row', 'Alder Court', 'Weft Street'). license_no is a plausible producer licence code (e.g. 'AV-PL-4471'). product_line is one of 'Personal Auto', 'Homeowners', 'Umbrella', 'Renters'. tier is one of exactly three values: Standard, Preferred, President's Council. direct_line is a fictional phone number. @Headshot holds the agreed prepped headshot filename for that agent (headshot_a1_final.jpg ... headshot_a9_final.jpg, in row order) so the merge drops the correct neutralized headshot into that card. @Seal holds the prepped seal filename mapped from tier: Standard -> seal_standard.svg, Preferred -> seal_preferred.svg, President's Council -> seal_presidents_council.png. @Wordmark holds the SAME vectorized wordmark file -- aldervale_wordmark.svg -- in EVERY row, so the merge drops the one shared masthead mark onto every card as a merge bind. Column names must exactly match the template merge fields and the three @image-path columns.
inputs.realism_notes: Nine rows => the merge must produce exactly nine finished cards (page-count = row-count gate). The @Headshot / @Seal / @Wordmark columns hold the filenames the agent must produce and upload under those exact names, so naming discipline is a real dependency. The tier->@Seal mapping means the President's Council rows resolve to the raster foil seal while Standard/Preferred rows resolve to the vector crests — proving the three image columns and the triage both land in the deliverable. Long names exercise the auto-fit name frame. Distinct tier values also guarantee at least one row of each seal type so both triage branches are exercised.

inputs.name: raw_agent_headshots_x9.zip
inputs.gen_prompt: A set of 9 REAL full-frame DSLR/mirrorless camera captures of insurance producers — upper-body corporate headshots of different fictional agents at a branch office, each ~4000-4500 px on the long edge (full-resolution stills straight off the camera before crop), each with a photographic 18% grey card clipped at one corner of the frame as a neutral reference, all against a similar neutral office backdrop. Shot across two branch open-days under mismatched light so no single correction fits: (1) cool blue LED ceiling-panel cast, frame tilted ~4 deg; (2) warm reception-tungsten cast, level; (3) greenish back-office fluorescent cast AND slightly underexposed, tilted ~3 deg; (4) an agent with a genuinely warm, deep complexion shot under clean near-neutral light so the grey card ALREADY reads neutral (the warmth is real skin, not a white-balance error), level; (5) overexposed near a bright window, highlights hot on the forehead, level; (6) strong cool blue window-shade cast AND dark/underexposed, tilted ~4 deg; (7) near-neutral but flat and low-contrast, level; (8) mixed warm-key/cool-fill, mildly off, tilted ~3 deg; (9) slightly warm and dull, level. Each portrait has real skin texture, hair detail and fabric, a candid corporate feel, no studio gloss, no CGI; the grey card is clearly visible and uncropped in every frame; rendered large (~4000-4500 px long edge) so there is headroom to crop the card out and still clear the print pixel floor by downscale only.
inputs.realism_notes: REAL-CAMERA capture at ~4000-4500 px long edge (NOT an AI-gen ~1024-1536 px raster) precisely so each 4:5 crop can fill the 40 x 50 mm photo window at >=300 DPI by DOWNSCALE ONLY — no upscaling anywhere in the chain. Deliberately mismatched (per-frame WB and exposure vary, in opposite directions) so a single blanket correction cannot fix the set — each frame needs its own decision measured to its in-frame 18% grey card, the free checkable neutral target (inputs are generated, so it costs nothing). Frame 4 is the skin-tone trap: its warmth is real complexion and its card is already neutral, so cooling it is wrong. Delivered as a zip of 9 individually addressable full-resolution JPEGs; the grey card is cropped out for the final card but retained on the neutralized master for grading.

inputs.name: seal_standard_flat.png
inputs.gen_prompt: A flat two-colour production-tier seal reading 'STANDARD' — solid deep-navy lettering and a simple laurel/roundel emblem on a solid single-colour block, high contrast, hard clean edges, no gradients, no sheen, no photographic texture, exported slightly oversized and off-centre with a thin margin. Looks like printable line art / a logo file.
inputs.realism_notes: Flat, high-contrast, solid-fill so image_vectorize yields a clean SVG after prep-before-trace (crop-to-bounds + crisp). One of the two seals that CAN become clean vector line art.

inputs.name: seal_preferred_flat.png
inputs.gen_prompt: A flat two-colour production-tier seal reading 'PREFERRED' — solid lettering and a simple emblem on a solid single-colour block, high contrast, hard clean edges, no gradients, no sheen, no photographic texture, exported a different non-square size from the STANDARD seal with a thin margin.
inputs.realism_notes: Second flat vector-ready seal; different export size from the STANDARD seal so the crop-to-bounds prep is genuinely needed to normalise both before tracing.

inputs.name: seal_presidents_council_foil.png
inputs.gen_prompt: A close-up PHOTOGRAPH of an embossed metallic-foil presentation seal reading 'PRESIDENT'S COUNCIL', shot on a dark leather surface: a raised gold-foil medallion with specular highlights, soft reflections, a debossed rim, subtle surface texture and smooth metallic gradients across the letters and field. Clearly a photographed glossy embossed object, not flat line art — full of gradients and sheen.
inputs.realism_notes: THE TRIAGE / TRAP asset. It looks like 'just another tier seal', but it is a photographed embossed metallic-foil surface full of gradients and specular sheen: feeding it to image_vectorize returns a flat, muddy silhouette that destroys the foil and the emboss. The correct treatment is crop-to-bounds -> image_remove_background to transparency -> keep as a high-resolution raster placed via @Seal. Getting it wrong is invisible in a thumbnail and only shows when the President's Council cards print flat and dead. The brief deliberately does NOT name which seal is the foil one — the agent must inspect and route it.

inputs.name: aldervale_wordmark_letterhead.png
inputs.gen_prompt: A flat scan of the 'Aldervale' wordmark printed on cream letterhead stock: a clean deep-navy (#17233A) wordmark with a small alder-leaf glyph to the left in a single flat colour, printed on slightly warm off-white paper (NOT transparent, NOT pure white). Rendered as a real scan — the whole mark sits very slightly rotated (~2 deg) on the scan bed, there is extra paper margin around it, and edges are a touch soft. Single flat ink colour, high contrast, no gradients, no metallic sheen, so that once cleaned it will vectorize cleanly.
inputs.realism_notes: Flat single-ink printed mark on off-white ground (NOT metallic, NOT gradient) so it CAN become clean vector — deliberately distinct from the foil seal so the triage decision is real. Scanned-on-paper (off-white ground, ~2 deg skew, margin, soft edges) forces genuine prep-before-trace: straighten, boost contrast/crispness, crop to the mark, knock the cream ground to transparency, THEN vectorize. IP-clean fictional brand mark.

outputs.name: Aldervale_ProducerCards_perAgent_x9.pdf
outputs.spec: Exactly nine press-ready 105 x 148 mm (A6) portrait producer counter cards — ONE single-record card per roster row (page-count = row-count = 9) — exported from the one-file-per-row InDesign data-merge with 3 mm bleed and crop marks at ~300 DPI; each card binds its agent_name/branch/license_no/product_line/tier/direct_line verbatim from the roster, drops that agent's grey-card-neutralized headshot into the 40 x 50 mm photo window via @Headshot (>=472 x 591 px so it prints >=300 DPI), drops the correct prepped tier seal into the 22 x 22 mm seal window via @Seal (vector crest for Standard/Preferred rows, transparent-ground foil raster for President's Council rows), and drops the shared vectorized wordmark into the masthead via @Wordmark — all three by merge bind, never free-form placement.

outputs.name: headshots_neutralized_x9
outputs.spec: Nine grey-card-neutralized, straightened agent headshots, delivered as the face-framed 4:5 crops (grey card cropped OUT) that bind into the cards, alongside their RETAINED pre-crop neutralized masters (the *_neutralized full-res frames, grey card still in frame) which the harness keeps as the neutrality-grading artifacts. Acceptance (grader-checked, two SEPARATE claims): (a) neutralisation is graded on the RETAINED pre-crop neutralized master of each frame (the *_neutralized output, its in-frame 18% grey card still present) — the card region reads a clean neutral (per-channel spread near zero) with the whole set matched to one shared white point, and true-to-skin (no face forced off its genuine complexion, in particular frame 4 whose warmth is real); (b) card-exclusion is checked separately on each delivered face-framed 4:5 crop (the *_final output that binds into that agent's card) — it is framed on the face with the grey card fully cropped OUT (no card pixels present), at >=472 x 591 px. The neutrality tolerance is never evaluated on the card-removed face crop. Accompanied by a report of the final white-balance and exposure move AND the final pixel size applied to each frame.

outputs.name: tier_seals_prepped
outputs.spec: The three production-tier seals prepped triage-correct: seal_standard.svg and seal_preferred.svg as clean vector line art traced only after crop-to-bounds + crisp prep, and seal_presidents_council.png as the photographed embossed-foil seal cropped and knocked to transparency then kept as a high-resolution raster (>=260 px square) — NOT vectorized, so the foil sheen and emboss survive to print.

outputs.name: aldervale_wordmark.svg
outputs.spec: Clean vector SVG of the Aldervale wordmark, traced only after the letterhead scan is straightened, crisped, cropped to the mark, and knocked to transparency — razor-sharp and skew-free at masthead scale with no captured cream paper ground, bound into every card's masthead via @Wordmark.

connector_workflow.note: Triage: this frame is tilted ~4 deg, so level it first. (Only the tilted frames 1/3/6/8 get straightened; the level frames skip this — deciding which is part of the job.)

Cool blue LED ceiling cast: WARM it (positive temperature) and set tint until the in-frame 18% grey card reads neutral (R=G=B), then set exposure/highlights/shadows so the card sits at mid-grey and skin reads true. Reason the exact temperature/exposure to THIS card — do NOT reuse another frame's numbers. Report the final move. Single primitive-built adjustments call (replaces the deprecated image_adjust_color_temperature / _highlights / _brightness_and_contrast / _vibrance_and_saturation).

Crop the grey card out and reframe on the face to the 40 x 50 mm (4:5) photo-window ratio, keeping the result at >=472 x 591 px so it clears the 300 DPI print floor. The pre-crop master (a1_neutralized, card still in frame) is RETAINED by the harness as the neutrality-grading artifact; neutrality is graded THERE, card-exclusion is the separate check on this crop. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only, never generative-expand. Report final px.

Warm reception-tungsten cast, level frame: this one must move the OPPOSITE direction from frame 1 — COOL it (negative temperature) until its grey card reads neutral and it matches the shared white point. Adaptive: the batch is not uniformly cool, so a blanket 'warm everything' pass fails here. Report the move.
Crop the card out, reframe to the 4:5 photo window at >=472 x 591 px. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. Report final px.
Tilted ~3 deg — level it before grading.

Greenish back-office fluorescent cast AND underexposed: the dominant colour move is on TINT (push toward magenta) to kill the green while neutralizing the grey card, plus a real exposure lift — a two-axis problem, not a simple temperature slide. Land the card neutral on the shared white point. Report the move.
Crop the card out, reframe to the 4:5 photo window at >=472 x 591 px. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. Report final px.

THE SKIN-TONE TRAP FRAME. This agent has a genuinely warm, deep complexion and was shot under clean near-neutral light, so the in-frame grey card ALREADY reads neutral. The correct move is essentially NO white-balance shift — only match exposure/brightness to the set. A naive agent that batch-applies the 'warm the cool cast' correction used on frames 1/8, or that 'cools an imagined cast', will neutralize the card off-neutral and strip the agent's real skin tone. Decision must be driven by THIS card, not the batch. Report that WB was held.
Crop the card out, reframe to the 4:5 photo window at >=472 x 591 px. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. Report final px.

Overexposed near a bright window with hot forehead highlights: PULL exposure/highlights/whites down to recover the blown skin first, then a small WB nudge so its grey card lands neutral on the shared white point. Tonal recovery dominates here. Report the move.
Crop the card out, reframe to the 4:5 photo window at >=472 x 591 px. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. Report final px.
Tilted ~4 deg — level it before grading.

Strong cool blue window-shade cast AND dark: warm STRONGLY and lift shadows/exposure to bring it up while neutralizing its grey card to the shared white point; protect skin from going muddy. The biggest correction in the set — proof that identical batch numbers cannot serve every frame. Report the move.
Crop the card out, reframe to the 4:5 photo window at >=472 x 591 px. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. Report final px.

Near-neutral light but flat and low-contrast, level: its grey card is already close to neutral, so only a SMALL WB nudge is needed to sit on the shared white point — over-correcting would push it off the set. The real work is tonal: add contrast/clarity and a touch of vibrance to match the set's feel without clipping. Report the (small WB, tonal) move.
Crop the card out, reframe to the 4:5 photo window at >=472 x 591 px. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. Report final px.
Tilted ~3 deg — level it before grading.
Mixed warm-key / cool-fill, only mildly off: a modest, careful correction to bring the grey card to neutral on the shared white point without overshooting. Report the move.
Crop the card out, reframe to the 4:5 photo window at >=472 x 591 px. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. Report final px.

Slightly warm and dull, level: cool a touch to neutralize its grey card to the shared white point and add vibrance/clarity to match the set. Report the move. Frames 1-9 now share one white point, each neutralized to its own grey card.
Crop the card out, reframe to the 4:5 photo window at >=472 x 591 px. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. Report final px.

Triage: the STANDARD seal is flat two-colour line art, so it CAN become clean vector. Prep-before-trace step 1: crop the oversized/off-centre export to the tight bounds of the seal so the trace sees only the crest, not the margin.
Prep-before-trace step 2: push contrast and set the black/white points so the two solid colours separate hard-edged — a soft or low-contrast raster traces into ragged, doubled edges.
Trace the prepared flat seal into a clean SVG so the STANDARD crest stays razor-sharp at the 22 mm seal window across every Standard-tier card.
The PREFERRED seal is also flat line art (different export size). Prep-before-trace step 1: crop to the tight bounds of the seal.
Prep-before-trace step 2: crisp the contrast/black point so the trace is clean-edged, matching the STANDARD seal's treatment.
Trace the prepared PREFERRED seal into a clean SVG for the Preferred-tier cards.

Triage DIVERGES here: the PRESIDENT'S COUNCIL seal is a PHOTOGRAPH of an embossed metallic-foil medallion — full of gradients, emboss and specular sheen — so it CANNOT become clean line art (vectorizing it would return a flat muddy silhouette and kill the foil). Crop only to the tight bounds of the seal; do NOT send it to image_vectorize. The brief never flags which seal this is — the routing is the agent's call.

Knock the dark leather surround to transparency so only the foil medallion remains, keeping every gradient, emboss shadow and highlight intact. remove_background -> transparency (NOT select->invert->fill, NOT a solid fill). This preserves the foil the vector path would have destroyed.

Square-crop/resize the transparent foil seal to the 22 x 22 mm (1:1) seal-window ratio at >=260 px square so it prints >=300 DPI. Kept as a high-resolution raster placed via @Seal for the President's Council rows. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.
Prep-before-trace step 1: the letterhead scan sits ~2 deg rotated on the bed — straighten so the vector edges are square. Feeding the raw skewed scan to vectorize would bake in the rotation.

Prep-before-trace step 2: push contrast/clarity and drop the cream paper toward white so the navy lettering separates hard from the ground — a soft low-contrast scan traces into ragged, doubled edges.
Prep-before-trace step 3: crop away the paper margin to the tight bounds of the mark so vectorize traces only the wordmark, not the letterhead field.

Prep-before-trace step 4: knock the cream paper ground to transparency so the trace captures the letterforms and alder-leaf glyph only, not a rectangle of paper. remove_background -> transparency (NOT select->invert->fill). The mark is a flat single-ink print (not metallic), so unlike the foil seal it survives — and belongs on — the vector path.

Now trace the prepared raster (straightened, crisped, cropped, transparent) into a clean SVG for the masthead. Tracing the raw scan instead would produce a skewed, paper-bounded, fuzzy silhouette — the trap this prep chain avoids.

connector_workflow.inputs_from: headshot_a1_final, headshot_a2_final, headshot_a3_final, headshot_a4_final, headshot_a5_final, headshot_a6_final, headshot_a7_final, headshot_a8_final, headshot_a9_final, seal_standard.svg, seal_preferred.svg, seal_presidents_council.png, aldervale_wordmark.svg
connector_workflow.note: Initialize an upload session for the nine grey-card-neutralized headshots, the three prepped tier seals and the vector wordmark so the merge can resolve them by the @Headshot, @Seal and @Wordmark columns. Files uploaded under the exact names the roster references.
Finalize the upload; returns the asset URNs the roster's @Headshot / @Seal / @Wordmark columns resolve to for each producer's single-record card.

One-file-per-row InDesign data-merge: bind each of the nine roster rows (agent_name/branch/license_no/product_line/tier/direct_line) into the authored SINGLE-RECORD .indd's live <<fields>> and resolve ALL THREE image columns per row — drop that row's neutralized headshot into the @Headshot frame, its mapped tier seal into the @Seal frame (vector crest for Standard/Preferred, transparent-ground foil raster for President's Council), and the shared vectorized wordmark (from @Wordmark, the same SVG in every row) into the masthead frame — producing EXACTLY ONE merged card per row (nine cards); the auto-fit name frame shrinks long names. Binding the wordmark/seal/headshot through the image columns is what places them: free-form image-at-coordinates placement is banned, so the merge is their only connector-doable path. [T] requires the hand-authored template. A convert_pdf_to_indd template or a multi-record table would not bind / cannot be produced — this is the corrected merge path that replaces the killed original's one-page rate table.

Export the merged single-record cards to press-ready ~300 DPI A6 (105 x 148 mm) + 3 mm bleed PDF with crop marks, one card per producer. document_render_layout exports the WHOLE merged multi-page document (all nine cards, one page per agent) in a single call — it cannot export one named record on its own, so any 'hero' agent is simply one page of this set, not a separate file. Acceptance: page-count = row-count = 9; if fewer, the merge collapsed rows and failed.

chaining_note: Strict output-to-input chaining throughout. Nine per-headshot grade sub-chains fan out from the raw zip, each an image_apply_adjustments neutralization (adaptive per frame: warm the cool LED frame 1, cool the tungsten frame 2, magenta-tint+lift the green/dark frame 3, HOLD white balance on the genuinely-warm-skin frame 4, recover the overexposed frame 5, strongly warm+lift the blue/dark frame 6, hold WB but add tone on the flat frame 7, modestly correct the mixed frame 8, cool+vibrance the warm/dull frame 9) followed by an image_crop_and_resize that crops the grey card out, reframes to the 4:5 photo window and holds >=472 x 591 px, with image_auto_straighten inserted only on the tilted frames 1/3/6/8 — every neutralization driven to that frame's own in-frame 18% grey card so all nine converge on one shared white point. The three tier seals TRIAGE into two paths: the flat STANDARD and PREFERRED crests each run crop_to_bounds -> crisp adjustments -> image_vectorize into clean SVGs (23->24->25, 26->27->28), while the photographed embossed-foil PRESIDENT'S COUNCIL seal diverges to crop_to_bounds -> image_remove_background (transparency) -> crop_and_resize into a high-res transparent raster (29->30->31), deliberately never touching image_vectorize.
